blockers.title: M11 MoSCoW text still says 'ignore stale/unknown/error responses' — directly contradicts M23/AC23 which require 'route unknown' + retry UI for unknown/error
blockers.description: M11 (ticket line 113) says: 'call /api/route with monotonic request_seq; display segment duration when status===ok; ignore stale/unknown/error responses'. M23 explicitly amends the AC layer: 'this AMENDS AC12 (which previously said ignore unknown/error responses — replace that clause with show unknown+retry)'. AC12 was correctly updated. But M11 in the MoSCoW Must-Have section was NOT updated — it still says 'ignore stale/unknown/error responses'. A dev reading the MoSCoW requirements list would implement the old behavior (ignore) for the M11 requirement, then encounter M23 amending AC12 but not M11, producing ambiguity about which governs.

evidence.m23_text: this AMENDS AC12 (which previously said ignore unknown/error responses — replace that clause with show unknown+retry) (ticket line 125)
evidence.ac12_amended: correctly updated to include unknown+retry cross-reference to AC23 (ticket lines 312-314)
evidence.conflict: M11 says ignore; M23/AC12/AC23 say render + retry. M11 was not updated when M23 was added.

blockers.proposed_fix: Update M11 to: 'display segment duration when status===ok; when status===unknown OR request fails, show unknown+retry per M23; discard responses with stale request_seq only'. Remove 'ignore unknown/error responses' from M11.

blockers.title: Technical Hint 12 says source key 'deleted' in slot-to-slot move — contradicts AC17's 'set to null' and would resurrect persisted selection under AC10 hasOwnProperty semantics
blockers.description: AC17 (ticket line 357) correctly specifies: 'slot A and slot B are updated in a single editorSelections state update: slot A key set to null'. Under AC10's hasOwnProperty semantics, key-absent triggers fallback to slot.selected_option_id (the persisted published value). Technical Hint 12 (ticket line 532) says: 'returns a new object with the source key deleted and the destination key set in one call'. If dev follows Hint 12 and DELETES the source key, the source slot will have no key in editorSelections, causing the hasOwnProperty resolver to fall back to the published selected_option_id (still set on the server), and the source slot will re-render as still selected. This is exactly the deselect semantics bug that B3 was meant to fix — Hint 12 reintroduces it.

evidence.ac17_text: slot A's key set to null (key present, value null = explicitly cleared) (ticket line 357)
evidence.hint12_text: returns a new object with the source key deleted and the destination key set in one call (ticket line 532)
evidence.ac10_resolver: Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(editorSelections, key) ? editorSelections[key] : slot.selected_option_id — absent key falls through to published value
evidence.conflict: Hint 12 'deleted' vs AC17 'null'. Deleted key = absent key = fallback to persisted value = source slot still shows as selected after slot-to-slot move.

blockers.proposed_fix: Update Technical Hint 12 to: 'returns a new object with the source key present and set to null (NOT deleted — absent key falls back to persisted value under AC10 hasOwnProperty semantics) and the destination key set to the option_id, in one functional update call'.

blockers.title: AC19 Meals selected state checks raw slot.selected_option_id — not the shared AC10 resolver — making explicit deselect/null invisible to the Meals sidebar
blockers.description: AC10 establishes that selected state is determined via the hasOwnProperty resolver: key present + null = explicitly cleared (slot renders unselected). AC19 (ticket line 378) says: 'a card is shown as selected (visual indicator) if ANY of breakfast/lunch/dinner has selected_option_id === card.option_id'. The term selected_option_id here refers to the raw slot data field, not the resolved value. If a user deselects a meal card (editorSelections[dayKey+':'+breakfast] = null), the raw slot.selected_option_id on the published day data may still be non-null. AC19's raw-field check would still show the card as selected, directly contradicting the AC10 deselect semantics and AC17 plan->candidates drag-to-deselect behavior. AC10 explicitly states 'this same resolver is used for effectiveDay merging, cover image, route, and budget inputs' — AC19 must use it too.

evidence.ac19_text: a card is shown as selected if ANY of breakfast/lunch/dinner has selected_option_id === card.option_id (ticket line 378)
evidence.ac10_shared_resolver: this same resolver is used for effectiveDay merging, cover image update, route gap inputs, and budget recompute inputs — it is a shared utility function (ticket line 295)
evidence.conflict: AC19 checks raw slot.selected_option_id; AC10 resolver checks editorSelections with hasOwnProperty. After deselect (editorSelections[key]=null), raw field still non-null, AC19 shows card as still selected.

blockers.proposed_fix: Update AC19 to: 'a card is shown as selected if ANY of breakfast/lunch/dinner has a resolved selected id (via the shared AC10 hasOwnProperty resolver applied to editorSelections) that equals card.option_id; null resolution means unselected'. The check MUST use the shared resolver, not the raw slot.selected_option_id field.

blockers.title: AC7 weakens HTTP 409 response requirement to '(or save error state is shown)' — allows dev to omit ConflictBanner for HTTP 409
blockers.description: M7 requires: 'ConflictBanner appears when response.status === 409 OR response JSON contains conflict === 409-soft'. This is unambiguous — ConflictBanner for both cases. AC7 (ticket line 270) reads: 'THEN ConflictBanner also appears (or save error state is shown)'. The parenthetical '(or save error state is shown)' is a disjunction — dev can implement HTTP 409 as save-error state only (no ConflictBanner) and satisfy AC7 literally while violating M7. The 409-soft case (HTTP 200) correctly requires ConflictBanner, but the HTTP 409 case is weakened. A dev could implement: 409-soft -> ConflictBanner, HTTP 409 -> generic error state — wrong user experience, violates M7.

evidence.m7_text: ConflictBanner appears when response.status === 409 OR response JSON contains conflict === 409-soft (ticket line 109)
evidence.ac7_409soft: THEN ConflictBanner appears offering a reload option (ticket line 268) — unambiguous
evidence.ac7_http409: THEN ConflictBanner also appears (or save error state is shown) (ticket line 270) — disjunction weakens requirement
evidence.conflict: M7 mandates ConflictBanner for HTTP 409. AC7's '(or save error state)' clause makes ConflictBanner optional for HTTP 409.

blockers.proposed_fix: Remove '(or save error state is shown)' from AC7 line 270. Update to: 'THEN ConflictBanner appears' — same unconditional requirement as the 409-soft case. ConflictBanner is mandatory for both HTTP 409 and 409-soft.

blockers.title: Missing required slot (absent key from effectiveDay) not explicitly defined as gating Approve/Export — Hint 19's 'if the slot exists' allows dev to skip absent required slots
blockers.description: AC24 gates on 'non-skipped slots in REQUIRED_SLOT_KEYS that have no selected_option_id'. AC22 defines a distinct 'missing' state for slots absent from effectiveDay entirely. Technical Hint 19 (ticket line 546) says: 'for each key in REQUIRED_SLOT_KEYS, get the slot from effectiveDay; if the slot exists and is not skipped and has no selected_option_id → not all filled'. The 'if the slot exists' clause means that if a required slot key is ABSENT from effectiveDay (missing state per AC22), the Hint 19 code would NOT flag it as unfilled — it would silently skip the absent slot and potentially enable Approve. A missing required accommodation or meal slot should clearly disable Approve and Export, but the spec does not state this.

evidence.hint19_code: for each key in REQUIRED_SLOT_KEYS, get the slot from effectiveDay; if the slot exists and is not skipped and has no selected_option_id → not all filled (ticket line 546)
evidence.ac22_missing_state: slot key absent from effectiveDay entirely → show missing status, data-droppable=false (ticket lines 400-404)
evidence.conflict: Hint 19's 'if slot exists' guard means absent required slot is not counted as unfilled, potentially allowing Approve with a missing accommodation or meal.

blockers.proposed_fix: Update Hint 19 and AC24 to explicitly state: 'a required slot that is ABSENT from effectiveDay (missing state per AC22) counts as unfilled and disables Approve/Export, in addition to slots that exist but have no selected_option_id'. Change Hint 19's condition to: 'if the slot is absent OR (slot exists AND not skipped AND no selected_option_id) → not all filled'.

blockers.title: AC11 budget recompute trigger 'drops a candidate' covers only candidates->plan direction — plan->candidates and slot->slot moves that change totals are excluded
blockers.description: M10 says: 'After each successful drop+save, POST /api/budget/recompute'. The word 'drop' could be read broadly, but AC11 (ticket line 299) says: 'WHEN a user successfully drops a candidate (POST /api/save returns 200)' — the phrase 'drops a candidate' implies candidates->plan direction only. Plan->candidates deselection and slot->slot moves both change the day's selected options and therefore the day total, and both involve a successful /api/save. Without recompute after these operations, the displayed budget total will be stale after any deselection or slot swap. A dev implementing AC11 literally would only recompute after candidates->plan drops.

evidence.m10_text: After each successful drop+save, POST /api/budget/recompute (ticket line 112) — ambiguous direction
evidence.ac11_text: WHEN a user successfully drops a candidate (POST /api/save returns 200) (ticket line 299) — implies candidates->plan only
evidence.missing_cases: plan->candidates deselect changes total (clears selection); slot->slot swap changes total (swaps selections); neither covered by 'drops a candidate'

blockers.proposed_fix: Update AC11 WHEN clause to: 'WHEN any selection-changing save completes successfully — candidates->plan drop, plan->candidates deselect, slot->slot move, or tap-to-select — and POST /api/save returns 200'.

warnings.title: Mobile breakpoint boundary ambiguity at exactly 768px — AC13 does not specify boundary-inclusive behavior
warnings.description: M12 says isMobileLayout = window.innerWidth < 768. AC13 tests at 390px (mobile) and 1440px (desktop) but does not specify what happens at exactly 768px. There is no test at the boundary (767px, 768px). A dev implementing with <= instead of < would pass all specified test widths but produce different behavior at the boundary.
warnings.proposed_fix: Add AC13 boundary test: 'GIVEN viewport width = 767px, THEN mobile layout active. GIVEN viewport width = 768px, THEN desktop layout active.'

warnings.title: Budget recompute stale-response guard scope (per-day vs global) unspecified
warnings.description: M10/M25 specify 'same stale-response guard (request_seq)' without clarifying whether request_seq is global or per-day. Both implementations are functionally acceptable; this is an implementation detail, not a spec contradiction.
warnings.proposed_fix: Clarify AC25: 'The stale-response guard is per-day (each day maintains its own monotonic request_seq for budget recompute)' or state 'global'. Either is acceptable.

warnings.title: AC1 verification command does not actually generate trip HTML bytes
